symptoms.symptom: Start status indicator light flashing

causes.label: The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted.
remedies: Press the Start pad once and close the door within 4 seconds to start the dishwasher.
Press the Start pad a second time when the dishwasher is running only if you wish to cancel the cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted."

symptoms.symptom: Dishwasher BEEPS once every minute (on some models)

causes.label: This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door.
remedies: Press Start and close the door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door."

symptoms.symptom: Beeping at the end of the cycle (on some models)

causes.label: This is normal. Dishwasher will beep twice at the end of the cycle.
remedies: To turn off the double beep indicator (or re-activate it if it was previously turned off), press the Heated Dry pad 5 times within 3 seconds.
A triple beep will sound to indicate the end-of-cycle beep option has been turned on or off.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "This is normal. Dishwasher will beep twice at the end of the cycle."

symptoms.symptom: Dishes and flatware not clean

causes.label: Ultra-Fine Filter or Fine Filter is clogged
remedies: See the Care and Cleaning section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Ultra-Fine Filter or Fine Filter is clogged"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see the USING THE DISHWASHER section).
Turn on the hot water faucet nearest the dishwasher, let run until the water temperature stops rising.
Then start the dishwasher and turn off the faucet.
This ensures the entering water is hot.
Select Wash Temp Boost if available.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Water pressure is temporarily low
remedies: Turn on a faucet.
Is water coming out more slowly than usual?
If so, wait until pressure is normal before using your dishwasher.
Normal water pressure to the dishwasher should be 20-120 psi.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Water pressure is temporarily low"

causes.label: Air gap or disposer clogged
remedies: Clean the air gap or flush the disposer.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Air gap or disposer clogged"

causes.label: High drain loop or air gap not installed
remedies: Refer to the Installation Instructions for proper drain line installation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "High drain loop or air gap not installed"

causes.label: Improper rack loading
remedies: Make sure large dishware does not block the detergent dispenser or the wash arms.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Improper rack loading"

causes.label: Poor performing detergent
remedies: Use a highly rated detergent such as Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Poor performing detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Spots and filming on glasses and flatware

causes.label: Extremely hard water
remedies: Use rinse agents such as Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid to prevent spots and prevent new film build-up.
If water is extremely hard, a softener may be required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Extremely hard water"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure water temperature is at least 120°F (49°C).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher
remedies: Load dishwasher as shown in the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher"

causes.label: Old or damp powder detergent
remedies: Make sure detergent is fresh.
Use a highly rated detergent such as Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Old or damp powder detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser empty
remedies: Refill with rinse agent such as Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Rinse agent dispenser empty"

causes.label: Too little or low performing detergent
remedies: Make sure you use the proper amount of highly rated detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Too little or low performing detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Cloudiness on glassware 49-55122-1

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get it clean.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Low performing phosphatefree detergent
remedies: See A white film on glassware, dishware and the interior in this TROUBLESHOOTING section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 19: "Low performing phosphatefree detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Suds in the tub

causes.label: Wrong detergent
remedies: Use only automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent has been approved for use in all GE Appliances dishwashers.
To remove suds from the tub, open the dishwasher and let suds dissipate.
Pump out water by pressing Start and close the door.
Wait 30 seconds.
Open the door, press and hold Start for 3 seconds, and close the door.
Repeat if necessary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Wrong detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Rinse agent was spilled"

symptoms.symptom: Detergent left in dispenser cups

causes.label: Dishes are blocking the detergent cup
remedies: Reposition the dishes, so the water from the lower spray arm can flush the detergent cup.
See the Loading section.
Reposition dishware that may be keeping the dispenser cup door from opening.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Dishes are blocking the detergent cup"

symptoms.symptom: Black or gray marks on dishes

causes.label: Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes
remedies: Remove marks with a mild, abrasive cleaner.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Aluminum utensils have rubbed against dishes"

symptoms.symptom: Dishes don’t dry Long cycle times

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is at least 120°F.
Select Heated Dry or Dry Boost.
Use Wash Temp Boost.
Select a higher cycle, such as Steam Sani or Heavy.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser is empty
remedies: Check the rinse agent dispenser and fill as required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Rinse agent dispenser is empty"

causes.label: Additional drying time is needed
remedies: Leave door closed after the Clean light appears to allow the fan to run an additional 90 minutes (on some models).
Note: If you open the door, this fan extension will be cancelled.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Additional drying time is needed"

causes.label: Cycle selection
remedies: If using Light cycle which uses lower water temperature and thus limited dry performance, switch to a different cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Cycle selection"

causes.label: Soil level
remedies: The turbidity sensor senses how much soil is on the dishes.
Heavy soiled dish loads will add more time to the cycle.
This is normal function.
For best wash and dry performance, allow cycle to complete.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Soil level"

symptoms.symptom: Control panel responded to inputs but dishwasher never filled with water

causes.label: Door may not be completely closed
remedies: Make sure the door is firmly closed.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Door may not be completely closed"

causes.label: Water valve may be turned off
remedies: Make sure water valve (usually located under the sink) is turned on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Water valve may be turned off"

causes.label: Flood float may be stuck
remedies: Remove Ultra-Fine filter and lightly tap the piece under the ultra fine filter that looks like a dome.
Replace the filter. 49-55122-1
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Flood float may be stuck"

symptoms.symptom: Stained tub interior

causes.label: Some tomato-based foods can cause reddish stains
remedies: Use of the Steam Sani cycle (on some models) after adding the dish to the load can decrease the level of staining.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Some tomato-based foods can cause reddish stains"

causes.label: Tea or coffee stains
remedies: Remove the stain by hand, using a solution of 1/2 cup bleach and 3 cups warm water.
NOTE: Do not use bleach on stainless steel inner door.
Before cleaning interior, wait at CAUTION least 20 minutes after a cycle for the heating elements to cool down.
Failure to do so can result in burns.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Tea or coffee stains"

causes.label: An overall yellow or brown film can be caused by iron deposits in water
remedies: A special filter in the water supply line is the only way to correct this problem.
Contact a water softener company.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "An overall yellow or brown film can be caused by iron deposits in water"

causes.label: White film on inside surface— hard water minerals
remedies: GE Appliances recommends Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid to help prevent hard water mineral deposits from forming.
Run dishwasher with citric acid to remove mineral deposits.
Citric acid (Part number: WD35X151) can be ordered through GE Appliances Parts.
See back cover for ordering information.
Alternatively, purchase Finish® Dishwasher Cleaner and follow the directions on the label.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "White film on inside surface— hard water minerals"

symptoms.symptom: Dishwasher won’t run

causes.label: Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
Remove any other appliances from the circuit.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped"

causes.label: Power is turned off
remedies: In some installations, the power to the dishwasher is provided through a wall switch, often located next to the disposer switch.
Make sure it is on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Power is turned off"

causes.label: Control panel is locked
remedies: Unlock control panel.
See the Getting started section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Control panel is locked"

symptoms.symptom: Control panel lights go off when you’re setting controls

causes.label: Time too long between touching of selected buttons
remedies: Each pad must be touched within 30 seconds of the others.
To relight, touch any pad again or open the door and unlock (top control).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Time too long between touching of selected buttons"

symptoms.symptom: Water standing in the bottom of the tub

causes.label: Air gap is clogged
remedies: Clean the air gap.
See the Care and Cleaning section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Air gap is clogged"

causes.label: High drain loop or air gap not installed
remedies: Refer to the Installation Instructions for proper drain line installation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "High drain loop or air gap not installed"

symptoms.symptom: Water won’t pump out of the tub 49-55122-1

causes.label: Drain is clogged
remedies: If you have an air gap, clean it.
See the Care and Cleaning section.
If the dishwasher drains into a disposer, run disposer clear.
Check to see if your kitchen sink is draining well.
If not, you may need a plumber. 21
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Drain is clogged"

symptoms.symptom: Steam

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: Warm, moist air comes through the vent during drying and when water is being pumped out.
This is necessary for drying.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "This is normal"

symptoms.symptom: Sanitized light does not illuminate at the end of the cycle

causes.label: The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during final rinse
remedies: Do not interrupt the cycle by opening the door during the wash cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The door was opened and the cycle was interrupted during final rinse"

causes.label: The incoming water temperature was too low
remedies: Raise the water heater temperature to between 120°F and 150°F.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "The incoming water temperature was too low"

symptoms.symptom: Noise

causes.label: Normal operating sounds:
remedies: These are all normal.
No action is required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Normal operating sounds:"

causes.label: Beeping at the end of the cycle (on some models)
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Beeping at the end of the cycle (on some models)"

causes.label: Rattling dishes when the spray arm rotates
remedies: Make sure dishes are properly loaded.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Rattling dishes when the spray arm rotates"

causes.label: Rattling silverware against door during wash
remedies: Tall utensils may be placed in the upper rack to avoid bumping against inner door during wash cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Rattling silverware against door during wash"

symptoms.symptom: A white film on glassware, dishware and the interior

causes.label: This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphate-free dishwasher detergent
remedies: To remove the white film, run your dishes through a dishwasher cycle with citric acid.
Use a WD35X151 citric acid kit found online.
Otherwise, use Finish® Dishwasher Cleaner found at your local grocery store.
Pour the citric acid in the detergent cup and close the cover.
Place the filmed but otherwise clean glassware and dishware in the dishwasher.
Leave silverware and other metal items out of the dishwasher.
Turn the dishwasher on and let it run through a complete cycle without detergent.
The glassware, dishware, and dishwasher should come out film free.
Alternatively, a vinegar rinse may be used.
Pour 1 cup of vinegar into dishwasher just after the detergent cup opens and let the dishwasher complete its cycle.
This may be repeated several times a year as needed.
The use of a rinse agent such as Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid may help minimize a repeat build up of film.
Also, the use of a highly rated detergent such as Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent will help prevent film build-up. 49-55122-1
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphate-free dishwasher detergent"
